name: Breast cancer (metastatic)
theme: goals change, honesty doesn't · the HER2-low rewrite

meta.title: Metastatic breast cancer in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Metastatic breast cancer (de novo stage IV or distant recurrence), adult
meta.population: Adults with metastatic breast cancer - the disease where goals change and honesty doesn't. Not curable with today's evidence, and measured in years for most subtypes: HR+/HER2- runs a median past five years with CDK4/6 inhibition, HER2+ nearly that on the CLEOPATRA-era backbone (and the DESTINY-Breast09 era just rewrote its first line), while TNBC's first line was rewritten twice in 2026 by TROP2 antibody-drug conjugates. HER2-low and ultralow are re-reads of yesterday's 'HER2-negative' - a fifth of those slides now route to a drug. Male MBC inside (ASCO guideline); leptomeningeal disease as a note; early-stage disease belongs to the live breast-early trainer.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the non-curable majority setting of the most common cancer in women. Every arm is control-intent and says so; the medians on the cards are real and belong to DIFFERENT trial populations - the cross-trial banner does more work here than anywhere else in this factory. Signature content: the CDK4/6 OS ledger (same class, three verdicts - only ribociclib's first-line OS is statistically significant); the HER2-low/ultralow rewrite (a pathology re-read of old negatives that unlocks T-DXd); the 2026 TNBC first-line rewrite (two TROP2 ADCs approved within five…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: Receptor-defined subtypes on METASTATIC tissue (re-biopsy: receptor conversion is real); ASCO/CAP ER/PR/HER2 with the HER2-low (IHC 1+/2+ ISH-) and HER2-ultralow (IHC 0 WITH membrane staining) re-read; ESMO MBC guideline 2026 as top-level anchor
meta.response: RECIST 1.1 on imaging; ctDNA monitoring is trial-grade, not standard - the SERENA-6 checkpoint teaches exactly why

Disease.label: Receptor subtype (on METASTATIC tissue)
Disease.help: Receptors can CHANGE between primary and metastasis - planning from the old report risks treating a tumor that no longer exists. The re-biopsy also enables the HER2-low/ultralow re-read.
Disease.helpPatient: The spread cancer gets its own biopsy, because its markers can differ from the original - and those markers choose the plan.

Disease.label: HER2-low / ultralow re-read (HER2-negative disease)
Disease.help: The rewrite of the decade: DB04 (HER2-low, post-chemo) and DB06 (low AND ultralow, post-endocrine) turned a re-read of old negatives into a therapy ticket - ultralow means IHC 0 with membrane stainin…
Disease.helpPatient: A pathologist re-examining an old 'negative' slide can now open a real treatment door - it costs a look, not a needle.

Disease.label: Visceral crisis
Disease.help: The exception that proves the endocrine-first rule: true visceral crisis (severe organ dysfunction needing rapid control) is the one HR+ scenario where chemotherapy still leads (guideline principle -…
Disease.helpPatient: Rarely, the cancer threatens an organ fast enough that the quickest-acting treatment goes first.

Disease.label: PD-L1 CPS (TNBC)
Disease.help: KEYNOTE-355 drew the line at CPS>=10 (OS 23.0 vs 16.1 only there), and the 2026 approvals kept it: SG+pembro at CPS>=10; Dato-DXd and SG-mono for the IO-ineligible.
Disease.helpPatient: One tissue score decides whether immunotherapy joins the first treatment.

Disease.label: ESR1 mutation (blood/tissue)
Disease.help: The resistance mutation that became a drug target three times over: elacestrant (2023), imlunestrant (2025-09), vepdegestrant - the first PROTAC degrader (2026-05) - all ESR1-mutant-restricted. Test…
Disease.helpPatient: A blood test at progression can reveal a resistance change that three newer tablets are designed for.

Disease.label: AKT-pathway alteration (PIK3CA / AKT1 / PTEN)
Disease.help: CAPItello-291's label is alteration-restricted (the FDA narrowed it to where the benefit concentrated: PFS 7.3 vs 3.1 in altered tumors). The ReDiscover-2 trial is asking the next-generation version…
Disease.helpPatient: A tumor-gene panel can open one more targeted-tablet door after the first treatments.

Disease.label: Germline BRCA1/2
Disease.help: PARP inhibitors beat chemotherapy on progression-free time and response in gBRCA carriers (OlympiAD PFS 7.0 vs 4.2, ORR 60% vs 29%; EMBRACA 8.6 vs 5.6) - overall survival did not separate, and the ca…
Disease.helpPatient: An inherited-gene test that can open a targeted-tablet option - and that relatives may want to know about.

Disease.label: Brain metastases
Disease.help: HER2+ brain metastases have two evidence-backed roads: the tucatinib triplet (HER2CLIMB - the first randomized intracranial win: CNS-PFS 9.9 vs 4.2) and T-DXd (DB12: 12-mo CNS-PFS 58.9%, single-arm).…
Disease.helpPatient: Spread to the brain changes which options lead - and this disease now has real ones there.

Newly diagnosed.name: Endocrine therapy + CDK4/6 inhibitor (the ledger told straight)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: ESMO MBC 2026 / NCCN (category secondhand - 403); endocrine-first unless visceral crisis
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x3 (one significant OS, one NS, one null - the ledger is the teaching)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the gentlest strong option in this factory: cytopenias (drug-specific), QT monitoring (ribociclib), diarrhea (abemaciclib) - tablet-based years
Newly diagnosed.patient: Tablets, not infusions, for the most common form of this disease - with a median past five years in the trial that proved survival, and normal-feeling life as the explicit goal.
drugs: Aromatase inhibitor + CDK4/6 inhibitor (ribociclib carries the OS claim)

Newly diagnosed.name: Chemotherapy first (visceral crisis - the exception that proves the rule)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: ESMO/ABC consensus principle (definition text secondhand this run - flagged)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: full chemotherapy season under organ-dysfunction conditions - the hardest version of this disease's start
Newly diagnosed.patient: When the cancer threatens an organ fast, the fastest-acting treatment goes first - and the gentler long-run plan takes over as soon as it safely can.
drugs: Taxane- or platinum-based chemotherapy, then endocrine maintenance

Newly diagnosed.name: T-DXd + pertuzumab (DESTINY-Breast09 - the new HER2+ first line, still young)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS met at interim; OS immature
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: nausea-forward ADC ledger plus the ILD discipline: cough/dyspnea gets same-week imaging, always
Newly diagnosed.patient: The newest first-line option: the guided-chemotherapy antibody plus the classic blocker - the longest disease control ever measured here, with the honest note that its survival ledger is still being written.

Newly diagnosed.name: THP (CLEOPATRA - the mature HER2+ backbone)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: a taxane season up front, then years of antibody-only maintenance; cardiac surveillance throughout
Newly diagnosed.patient: The proven backbone: chemotherapy plus two antibodies at the start, then years of antibody-only maintenance - nearly five years median survival, with a decade of follow-up behind it.

Newly diagnosed.name: Pembrolizumab + chemotherapy (KEYNOTE-355 - the CPS>=10 survival anchor)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - OS met in CPS>=10
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: chemotherapy backbone plus immune-related events (thyroid foremost, some permanent)
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the subset whose tumor shows the immune marker: immunotherapy woven into chemotherapy, with a proven survival gain.

Newly diagnosed.name: Sacituzumab govitecan + pembrolizumab (ASCENT-04 - the 2026 CPS>=10 rewrite, still young)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS met; OS immature
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: neutropenia and diarrhea (the SG signature) plus immune-related events
Newly diagnosed.patient: The newest combination for the immune-marker subset: a guided chemotherapy plus immunotherapy - longer control proven, longer life still being measured.

Newly diagnosed.name: Datopotamab deruxtecan (TROPION-Breast02 - the IO-ineligible card with the OS receipt)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS and OS met
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: stomatitis and dry eye (the Dato signatures), ILD vigilance (deruxtecan class) - no treatment-related deaths in the trial
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the majority whose tumor lacks the immune marker: a guided chemotherapy that proved both longer control and longer life over standard chemo.

Newly diagnosed.name: Sacituzumab govitecan monotherapy (ASCENT-03 - PFS-proven, OS pending)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS met; OS immature (crossover critique noted)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: neutropenia and diarrhea, managed with an upfront plan
Newly diagnosed.patient: The other new option for the same group: proven to hold the cancer back longer than chemotherapy, with the longer-life question still being answered.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.evidence: historical series (teaching estimate, flagged); early-integration randomized
Newly diagnosed.patient: Choosing comfort alone is a real option with real numbers - and choosing treatment never means giving comfort up; here they run together from the start.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Oral degrader trio for ESR1-mutant disease (elacestrant / imlunestrant / vepdegestrant)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized x3 (PFS primary each; modest absolute medians - stated plainly)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the gentlest 2L family: nausea, fatigue, lipids (drug-specific) - tablets
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: If the resistance change is found, three approved tablets are built for exactly it - honest note: they buy months of control on average, gently, and keep chemotherapy in reserve.
drugs: Elacestrant / imlunestrant / vepdegestrant (per availability and profile)

Relapsed / recurrent.name: AKT-pathway card (capivasertib-fulvestrant; alpelisib/everolimus lineage)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized (PFS primary; label narrowed to where benefit concentrated)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: hyperglycemia, rash, diarrhea - the pathway class's metabolic ledger; glucose monitoring rides along
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For tumors carrying a growth-pathway change (four in ten do): a targeted tablet pair that roughly doubles control time in exactly those tumors.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: T-DXd for HER2-low/ultralow (the re-read's reward)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 - OS met (DB04), PFS met at the earlier position (DB06)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: nausea-forward; the ILD vigilance rule is absolute: new cough or breathlessness gets same-week imaging
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A second look at an old 'negative' slide can open this door: a guided chemotherapy that beat standard chemo on survival itself for tumors with even faint HER2 presence.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: T-DXd, HER2+ later line (DESTINY-Breast03 - the mature rout)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS and OS met, mature
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: nausea-forward ADC ledger; ILD vigilance absolute
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The guided-chemotherapy antibody that routed the previous standard - holding the cancer back four times longer in its trial, with a survival gain now mature.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Tucatinib + trastuzumab + capecitabine (HER2CLIMB - the brain-active triplet)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN preferred for HER2+ brain metastases (secondhand, congress-deck-sourced)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized incl. active brain mets - OS and CNS-PFS met
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: diarrhea and hand-foot (capecitabine's ledger), hepatic monitoring - an oral-backbone triplet
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The combination that proved itself where it is hardest - including cancer that has reached the brain, where it was the first to win a randomized test.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: T-DM1 (EMILIA - the relegated veteran, still real)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized (mature; head-to-head relegated by DB03)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the gentlest HER2 ADC: thrombocytopenia and LFTs - no ILD discipline needed at DB03 rates
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The earlier guided antibody - beaten head-to-head by the newer one, but gentler, and still a genuinely useful card later in the sequence.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Sacituzumab govitecan, TNBC later line (ASCENT - the original receipt)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: neutropenia and diarrhea, managed with an upfront plan
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The guided chemotherapy that nearly doubled survival in previously treated triple-negative disease.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: PARP inhibitor for gBRCA (OlympiAD/EMBRACA - control, honestly labeled)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 - PFS/ORR met; OS not significant
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: anemia and nausea; a tablet-based line with chemotherapy held in reserve
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For inherited-BRCA carriers: a tablet that works twice as often as chemotherapy and holds the cancer longer - honest label: it has not been shown to lengthen life, and the card says so.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Atezolizumab + nab-paclitaxel - WITHDRAWN: the ledger's standing mirror
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NOT available for TNBC in the US since 2021-08 (withdrawn)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: accelerated approval withdrawn after confirmatory failure
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: historical ledger: immune events plus taxane neuropathy
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: This combination is no longer offered - its confirming trial failed and the approval was given back. The card stays visible because several of today's newest options are at exactly the stage this one was, and honesty means showing both endings.
drugs: Atezolizumab + nab-paclitaxel - withdrawn in this indication

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort with symptoms managed well - a decision made openly at any line, never by drift.

refs.label: de Azambuja et al. Metastatic breast cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline. Ann Oncol 2026;37:1203-19 - the top-level guideline anchor (abstract-less record; content details secondhand). Predecessor: Gennari 2021
Cardoso et al. ABC 5 international consensus guidelines for advanced breast cancer (visceral-crisis and endocrine-first principles; definition wording secondhand this run). Ann Oncol 2020;31:1623-49

Wolff et al. HER2 testing ASCO/CAP 2023 update - binary reporting reaffirmed; the low/ultralow clinical story is carried by DB04/DB06 and the 2025 CDx expansion, not a guideline category. JCO 2023;41:3867-72
Hortobagyi et al. MONALEESA-2 final OS (ribociclib + letrozole, 1L): 63.9 vs 51.4 months (HR 0.76, p=0.008) - the class's only significant first-line OS. NEJM 2022;386:942-50
Goetz et al. MONARCH 3 final OS (abemaciclib + NSAI, 1L): 66.8 vs 53.7 months - NOT statistically significant (HR 0.804, p=0.066). Ann Oncol 2024;35:718-27

Slamon et al. PALOMA-2 final OS (palbociclib + letrozole, 1L): 53.9 vs 51.2 months, null (HR 0.96) - with the paper's own informative-censoring caveat (13.3% vs 21.2% unknown status). JCO 2024;42:994-1000
Bidard et al. EMERALD (elacestrant vs SOC endocrine, post-CDK4/6): PFS HR 0.55 in ESR1-mutant disease - the first oral SERD approval (2023-01, ESR1-restricted; date secondhand). JCO 2022;40:3246-56

Imlunestrant (EMBER-3): ESR1-mutant PFS 5.5 vs 3.8 months (HR 0.62); FDA approval 2025-09-25 as Inluriyo, ESR1-mutant-restricted (sponsor/press-corroborated; primary paper PMID pending verification - manifest item)

Vepdegestrant (VERITAC-2): first PROTAC ER degrader - ESR1-mutant PFS 5.0 vs 2.1 months vs fulvestrant; FDA approval 2026-05-01 with Guardant360 CDx (fda.gov-listed via search; primary paper pending verification - manifest item)

Bidard, Turner et al. SERENA-6 (camizestrant switch at ctDNA ESR1 emergence, pre-progression): PFS 16.0 vs 9.2 months (HR 0.44); time-to-QoL-deterioration also improved; 3,256 screened for 315 randomized. NEJM 2025;393:569-80

The SERENA-6 regulatory divergence (all secondhand, multiply corroborated): FDA ODAC voted 6-3 AGAINST clinical benefit of the pre-progression switch (2026-04-30; OS immature, no crossover); FDA decision date extended ~2026-05-27, still pending 2026-08; EU CHMP positive 2026-05-22 and cleared - the live case study in what a surveillance signal is worth

Turner et al. CAPItello-291 (capivasertib + fulvestrant, post-endocrine): overall PFS 7.2 vs 3.6; AKT-pathway-altered 7.3 vs 3.1 - the label is alteration-restricted (2023-11, secondhand). NEJM 2023;388:2058-70
Andre et al. SOLAR-1 (alpelisib + fulvestrant, PIK3CA-mutant): PFS 11.0 vs 5.7 (HR 0.65); no benefit without the mutation. NEJM 2019;380:1929-40
Baselga et al. BOLERO-2 (everolimus + exemestane, post-NSAI): PFS 6.9 vs 2.8 months - the pathway lineage's founder. NEJM 2012;366:520-9

Kalinsky et al. postMONARCH (abemaciclib + fulvestrant after CDK4/6 progression): PFS 6.0 vs 5.3 (HR 0.73; BICR 0.55) - continuation buys landmark-rate separation, not median separation; stated plainly. JCO 2025;43:1101-12

Modi et al. DESTINY-Breast04 (T-DXd, HER2-low post-chemo): PFS 9.9 vs 5.1, OS 23.4 vs 16.8 (HR 0.64) - the trial that retired 'HER2-negative' as a therapeutic category; ILD 12.1% (0.8% fatal). NEJM 2022;387:9-20

Bardia et al. DESTINY-Breast06 (T-DXd after endocrine therapy, HER2-low AND ultralow - IHC 0 with membrane staining): PFS 13.2 vs 8.1 (HR 0.62); FDA 2025-01-27 with Ventana 4B5 CDx expansion (dates secondhand). NEJM 2024;391:2110-22

Swain et al. CLEOPATRA end-of-study (docetaxel + trastuzumab/pertuzumab, 1L HER2+): OS 57.1 vs 40.8 months (HR 0.69), 8-yr OS 37% - the mature backbone (the 2015 interim was 56.5; end-of-study is the citable figure). Lancet Oncol 2020;21:519-30

Tolaney et al. DESTINY-Breast09 (T-DXd + pertuzumab vs THP, 1L HER2+): PFS 40.7 vs 26.9 months (HR 0.56, interim), ORR 85.1%; ILD 12.1% incl. two fatal; OS immature. US approval 2025-12-15 (secondhand). NEJM 2025;394:551-62
Cortes et al. DESTINY-Breast03 (T-DXd vs T-DM1, 2L): PFS HR 0.28 - the rout. NEJM 2022;386:1143-54; OS update (Hurvitz, Lancet 2023;401:105-17): HR 0.64
Cortes et al. DESTINY-Breast03 mature analysis (41-month follow-up): median OS 52.6 vs 42.7 (HR 0.73); PFS 29.0 vs 7.2 (HR 0.30); ILD 16.7% with no new grade >=3. Nat Med 2024;30:2208-15
Curigliano et al. HER2CLIMB final OS (tucatinib + trastuzumab + capecitabine): 24.7 vs 19.2 months (HR 0.73). Ann Oncol 2022;33:321-9

Lin et al. HER2CLIMB intracranial results - the first randomized CNS win in HER2+ MBC: CNS-PFS 9.9 vs 4.2 (HR 0.32), intracranial ORR 47.3% vs 20.0%, OS benefit in brain-mets patients (HR 0.58). JCO 2020;38:2610-9

Harbeck et al. DESTINY-Breast12 (T-DXd with stable or ACTIVE brain metastases, single-arm n=504): 12-mo PFS 61.6%, 12-mo CNS-PFS 58.9%; ILD 16% - prospective CNS evidence, not randomized; the oft-quoted CNS ORR is secondary-analysis material, not carried here. Nat Med 2024
Verma et al. EMILIA (T-DM1 vs lapatinib-capecitabine): OS 30.9 vs 25.1 (HR 0.68) - the veteran DB03 relegated but did not retire. NEJM 2012;367:1783-91
Cortes et al. KEYNOTE-355 final OS (pembrolizumab + chemo, 1L TNBC): CPS>=10 OS 23.0 vs 16.1 (HR 0.73, p=0.0185); no significant benefit below the boundary. NEJM 2022;387:217-26
Bardia et al. ASCENT (sacituzumab govitecan, 2L+ TNBC): PFS 5.6 vs 1.7, OS 12.1 vs 6.7 (HR 0.48) - the ADC arrival in TNBC. NEJM 2021;384:1529-41

Tolaney et al. ASCENT-04/KEYNOTE-D19 (SG + pembrolizumab vs chemo + pembrolizumab, 1L CPS>=10): PFS 11.2 vs 7.8 (HR 0.65), DOR 16.5 vs 9.2; OS immature. Approved 2026-06-24 (secondhand). NEJM 2026;394:354-66

Cortes et al. ASCENT-03 (SG monotherapy vs chemo, 1L IO-ineligible): PFS 9.7 vs 6.9 (HR 0.62); OS immature, with a published crossover-adjustment critique the card carries. Approved 2026-06-24 (secondhand; encode n=558 per paper, not the registry's 623). NEJM 2025;393:1912-25

Dent et al. TROPION-Breast02 (Dato-DXd vs chemo, 1L IO-ineligible TNBC): PFS 10.8 vs 5.6 (HR 0.57) AND OS 23.7 vs 18.7 (HR 0.79, p=0.029) - the 1L rewrite that arrived with its survival receipt; no treatment-related deaths. Approved 2026-05-22 (secondhand). Ann Oncol 2026;37:1066-80
Robson et al. OlympiAD (olaparib vs chemo, gBRCA HER2-): PFS 7.0 vs 4.2 (HR 0.58), ORR 59.9% vs 28.8%; final OS did not separate - the card displays response and says so. NEJM 2017;377:523-33
Litton et al. EMBRACA (talazoparib vs chemo, gBRCA): PFS 8.6 vs 5.6 (HR 0.54); final OS not significant. NEJM 2018;379:753-63

Atezolizumab + nab-paclitaxel in PD-L1+ mTNBC: accelerated approval (2019, IMpassion130 PFS) VOLUNTARILY WITHDRAWN 2021-08-27 after confirmatory IMpassion131 failed - the standing mirror for PFS-led approvals (sponsor statement; secondary corroboration)

NRG-BR002 (SOC +/- SBRT/surgical ablation of oligometastases, <=4 mets): futility met - PFS 19.5 vs 23.0 months, HR 0.92 (one-sided p=0.36); the phase 3 OS question never opened. HONESTY NOTE: no PubMed-indexed full paper exists - the ASCO 2022 abstract (Chmura et al) and the registry's posted results are the citable records

Stopeck et al. Denosumab vs zoledronic acid for bone metastases in advanced breast cancer (randomized) - the bone-agent anchor; effect-size figure pending abstract re-pull (flagged). JCO 2010;28:5132-9

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.
